photos.groupLabel: Easy: portraits
photos.title: [Portrait of Harriet Tubman]
photos.description: The main subject is a woman standing indoors, identified by the catalog title as a portrait of Harriet Tubman. She is standing next to a small upholstered chair with her hands resting on the back of it. She wears a long dark dress with a white collar at the neck and long sleeves, and flat shoes. A dark shawl or coat is draped over the arm of the chair, and a hat rests on the seat. To her left there is a small table covered with a dark cloth. Behind her is a plain wall and a vertical column or door trim. The image is a black and white studio portrait with a patterned carpet on the floor.
photos.estimatedPeriod: 1895 per catalog date, consistent with clothing and photographic style.
notableDetails: woman with hands clasped on chair back
long dark dress with white collar
tassel hanging from chair
photos.reference: Photograph shows a full-length portrait of Harriet Tubman (1820?-1913) looking directly at the camera with folded hands resting on back of an upholstered chair.

photos.title: Neon sign, Westchester Ave., Bronx, Oct. 1970
photos.description: A large weathered neon sign shaped like a ring with a clock in the center. The sign reads BLOOM JEWELER in large raised letters around a round clock face. The sign is designed to look like a diamond ring, with a large faceted diamond shape at the top and a circular band below. The clock in the middle has black numerals and white hands showing about 5 and 13 minutes past 2. The paint is peeling and some neon tubes are broken or missing, and the metal frame is rusted. The sign is mounted on the side of a light-colored building, photographed from below against a bright sky. The image is in color. Estimated from catalog date as 1970.
notableDetails: Sign shaped like a diamond ring with clock
Text reads BLOOM JEWELER
Visible wear, rust, and missing neon

photos.groupLabel: Medium: signs and text in the photo
photos.title: Sign at entrance of Castle Clinton
photos.description: A rectangular informational sign mounted on a wooden fence at the entrance of Castle Clinton. The sign reads CASTLE CLINTON NATIONAL MONUMENT REMAINS OF WAR OF 1812 FORT WHICH LATER BECAME THE FAMOUS CASTLE GARDEN, THEATRE AND EMIGRANT LANDING DEPOT, AND FINALLY, THE NEW YORK CITY AQUARIUM. RESTORATION OF FORT RUINS BEGAN IN OCTOBER 1950. WORK WILL CONTINUE AS FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE. NATIONAL PARK SERVICE UNITED STATES DEPT. OF INTERIOR. The sign has white lettering on a dark background with a light border. It is attached to vertical wooden planks, with rough stone blocks visible above the fence. The photograph is black and white and mounted on a light mat with dark corners. Estimated from catalog date as 1952.
notableDetails: Sign explains history of Castle Clinton and restoration starting October 1950
Mounted on wooden fence with stone above
Black and white print with mat border
photos.reference: Photograph shows sign that reads "Castle Clinton National Monument. Remains of War of 1812 fort which later became the famous Castle Garden, theatre and emigrant landing depot, and finally, the New York City Aquarium. Restoration of fort ruins began in October 1950. Work will continue as funds are available. - National Park Service United States Dept. of Interior".

photos.groupLabel: Hard: bird's-eye views, prints and maps
photos.title: Bird's-eye view of Philadelphia / drawn and engraved expressly for Harper's Weekly from sketches by Theodore R. Davis.
photos.description: Photo 1 is a black-and-white bird's-eye view engraving of Philadelphia. Text at the top reads SUPPLEMENT TO HARPER'S WEEKLY, June 15, 1872. Text at the bottom center reads BIRD'S-EYE VIEW OF PHILADELPHIA. Text at the bottom left reads Drawn and Engraved Expressly for Harper's Weekly. Text at the bottom right reads From Sketches by Theodore R. Davis. The view looks north over a dense grid of city blocks extending to the horizon. At the bottom foreground is a wide river with many sailing ships, steamboats, and small boats. A bridge with stone arches crosses the river on the lower left. The city is filled with rows of low buildings, with taller church steeples and larger structures scattered throughout. Two small islands with trees are in the river. In the far background a second river curves across the top of the image with open fields beyond.
photos.estimatedPeriod: 1872, which matches the catalog date and the printed date of June 15, 1872 visible at the top of the image.
notableDetails: The title BIRD'S-EYE VIEW OF PHILADELPHIA is printed at the bottom center.
The river in the foreground is the Delaware River with numerous ships and boats.
The image is marked as a supplement to Harper's Weekly.
The city is shown as a dense, regular street grid viewed from above.
photos.reference: Print shows a bird's-eye view of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, with the Delaware River, Windmill Island, and Smith Island in the foreground, and the Schuylkill River in the background; streets and prominent features identified on print.

photos.title: View of the ruins of the city of Pittsburgh from Boyd's Hill / painted by W.C. Wall ; on stone by James Queen ; lith. of Wagner & McGuigan, No. 100, Chesnut Street, Philada.
photos.description: Photo 2 is a lithograph showing a city in ruins after a fire. Text at the bottom reads VIEW of the RUINS of the CITY of PITTSBURGH from BOYD'S HILL. Smaller text at the bottom left reads Painted by W.C. Wall. Smaller text at the bottom right reads On stone by James Queen. Smaller text at the bottom center reads Lith. of Wagner & McGuigan, No. 100, Chesnut Street, Philada. The viewpoint is from a high hill looking down a long straight street lined on both sides by burnt-out buildings, with only walls and chimneys standing. In the foreground a paved road with a stone retaining wall and lampposts curves down the hill, where a few small figures of people are walking. In the middle distance a church steeple remains standing intact. Beyond the ruins a river is visible on the left, and tree-covered hills are in the background under a cloudy sky.
photos.estimatedPeriod: 1850 per the catalog date, which is consistent with the lithographic style and clothing of the figures.
notableDetails: The printed title VIEW of the RUINS of the CITY of PITTSBURGH from BOYD'S HILL is visible at the bottom.

Several small human figures are scattered on the streets and on the hill road in the foreground.
photos.reference: Print shows a bird's-eye view of the ruins of the city of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania after the fire of April 10, 1845.

photos.title: Topographic view of the city of Reading Pa. 1881 / compiled from sketches by J. Hanold Kendall, and dedicated to its growing industries.
photos.description: Photo 5 is a illustrated topographic view of a city surrounded by inset images of buildings. Large text near the center top reads TOPOGRAPHIC VIEW OF THE CITY OF and large text near the center bottom reads READING PA. 1881. Smaller text at the top border reads SITUATED IN THE MIDST OF A RICH MINERAL & AGRICULTURAL DISTRICT AND BECOME A LARGE MANUFACTURING CENTRE and at the far top left POPULATION and at the far top right 45,000. The central image is a bird's-eye view of a city in a river valley with dense blocks of buildings, many factory chimneys with smoke, and two bridges crossing a river in the foreground. Hills are visible in the background. Around the border are about twenty smaller inset illustrations of individual factories, churches, stores, and other buildings, each with small labels. Trees in the center foreground are near the river. The overall image is a black-and-white engraving with aged paper tones.
photos.estimatedPeriod: 1881, which matches the catalog date and the date READING PA. 1881 printed in the image.
